title: Industrial Distribution
summary: B2B value-added distributors of industrial components, MRO supplies, and specialized parts where working capital velocity and pricing matrices drive profitability.
businessModel: Purchasing industrial goods in bulk from manufacturers, holding inventory locally, and selling in smaller quantities to end-users (contractors, factories, mechanics).
revenueModel: Transactional, high-frequency B2B sales with margins generated by the spread between bulk purchasing costs and customized, rapid-delivery pricing.
costStructure: Cost of Goods Sold (inventory purchasing), facility leasing (warehouses/branches), logistics (freight and delivery fleets), and sales rep commissions.
keyKpis: Revenue per Branch / Revenue per Rep
whyPeLikesIt: Massively fragmented markets, highly recession-resilient (MRO is non-discretionary), sticky B2B relationships, and the ability to drive massive cash flow through working capital optimization.
investmentThesis: Roll up regional distributors to achieve purchasing scale, implement robust ERP systems to optimize inventory velocity, overhaul pricing matrices to capture margin on 'C-parts', and shift analog branch sales to B2B e-commerce.
diligenceQuestions: What is the true rate of obsolete or 'dead' inventory hiding on the balance sheet?
How much pricing authority do individual sales reps have to discount products?
What percentage of revenue is highly sticky MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Operations) versus cyclical CapEx projects?
operationalIssues: Sales reps arbitrarily discounting products, destroying gross margin.
Millions of dollars tied up in slow-moving or obsolete inventory.
Highly manual, analog purchasing processes resulting in frequent stockouts of critical items.
valueCreationLevers: Strategic pricing matrices and discount control
Branch footprint rationalization and network density
aiOpportunities: AI-driven demand forecasting to optimize inventory stocking levels by branch.
Dynamic pricing algorithms that adjust margins based on customer size and order frequency.
Automated product cross-referencing to find cheaper alternative SKUs for customers.
risks: Amazon Business or aggressive digital disruptors stealing market share.
Severe supply chain disruptions or sudden deflation in commodity parts.
Loss of key sales reps who hold tight relationships with major buyers.
Over-leveraging the balance sheet if inventory turns slow down.
hundredDayPlan: Lock down the ERP to prevent unauthorized sales discounting.
Identify and liquidate obsolete inventory to immediately free up cash.
Consolidate purchasing across the portfolio to renegotiate vendor rebates.
exitReadiness: A highly optimized, multi-region hub-and-spoke distribution network.
A significant percentage of revenue flowing through a low-touch B2B e-commerce portal.
Industry-leading Return on Net Assets (RONA) proving capital efficiency.

articleSections.title: Pricing Matrices and the 'C-Part' Margin
body: In industrial distribution, gross margin is frequently destroyed by a pervasive culture of 'cowboy sales reps.' In founder-owned businesses, reps are often compensated purely on top-line revenue volume and are given the authority to arbitrarily discount products to close a deal. This results in horrific margin leakage. The core Private Equity playbook involves locking down the ERP system and replacing discretionary discounting with highly structured, data-driven 'Pricing Matrices.' This enforces discipline and ensures the company is paid appropriately for the logistical value it provides.

We optimize these matrices by analyzing the velocity and strategic value of the inventory. Fast-moving, highly competitive 'A-parts' (like major power tools) are priced sharply to win the business. However, the true profit engine of distribution lies in the 'C-parts'—inexpensive, slow-moving items like specialized washers, nuts, or obscure safety gear. Customers are entirely price-insensitive to a $2 bag of bolts when it prevents a $100,000 factory line shutdown. By systematically raising prices on tens of thousands of these C-parts, we can radically expand the blended gross margin.

The financial impact of this pricing discipline is immense. For a $300M distributor operating on a 25% gross margin, a highly targeted, algorithmic pricing strategy that lifts the blended margin by just 200 basis points yields $6M in pure, flow-through EBITDA. We expect the Operating Partner to establish strict approval workflows for any pricing exceptions and to restructure sales commissions to reward gross profit dollars rather than empty top-line revenue.
articleSections.callout: In distribution, you win the customer on the highly competitive A-parts, but you make your EBITDA on the invisible, high-margin C-parts.

articleSections.title: Working Capital Velocity and Inventory Optimization
body: Distribution is ultimately a game of capital allocation. A distributor's primary asset is its inventory, and its primary operational sin is allowing that inventory to stagnate. Many target companies suffer from millions of dollars tied up in 'dead' or obsolete stock—products sitting on shelves gathering dust because purchasing managers bought in massive bulk to secure a minor discount, completely ignoring the cost of capital. We attack this by obsessively optimizing 'Inventory Turns' and the cash conversion cycle.

We implement sophisticated demand forecasting tools within the ERP to shift the purchasing model from reactive 'gut feel' ordering to precise, algorithm-driven replenishment. We establish 'hub-and-spoke' network designs, centralizing slow-moving inventory in a single massive regional distribution center while keeping only high-velocity, fast-turning items at local branches. This ensures high 'Fill Rates' for the customer while dramatically reducing the total working capital required to support the revenue base.

Maximizing 'Return on Net Assets' (RONA) is the ultimate benchmark of distribution excellence. If we can increase inventory turns from 3x to 5x annually on a $50M inventory base, we instantly liberate $20M in trapped cash. This freed-up working capital is the lifeblood of the PE model; it is immediately deployed to pay down expensive debt or fund the acquisition of the next tuck-in competitor. A distributor with high inventory velocity is a highly resilient, cash-generating machine.

articleSections.title: Procurement Scale and Vendor Rebates
body: The fragmentation of the industrial distribution market presents a massive opportunity for procurement arbitrage. When a PE sponsor executes a roll-up strategy—acquiring five or six regional distributors—they suddenly control a significantly larger purchasing volume than any of the individual companies did historically. We immediately leverage this aggregated scale during the first 100 days to force major manufacturing suppliers (like 3M, DeWalt, or Honeywell) back to the negotiating table.

We demand not only lower unit costs but also highly structured, lucrative 'Vendor Rebate' programs. These rebates are often tiered, providing retroactive cash payments to the distributor if specific annual volume targets are hit. Because these rebate checks are typically accounted for as a reduction in Cost of Goods Sold, they drop directly to the bottom line as pure EBITDA. In mature distribution platforms, vendor rebates can constitute a shocking percentage of total enterprise profitability.

To maximize this lever, we actively manage 'Supplier Rationalization.' If a platform is buying safety gloves from 14 different vendors across its newly acquired branches, we consolidate that spend down to two preferred partners. By funneling all volume to those select suppliers, we easily trigger the highest tier of rebate thresholds. This procurement discipline ensures that the platform is extracting maximum financial value from its scale, creating an unassailable cost advantage over smaller, local competitors.

articleSections.title: Digital Transformation and B2B E-Commerce
body: The existential threat to traditional industrial distribution is the relentless encroachment of digital behemoths like Amazon Business. Legacy distributors relying entirely on analog processes—customers faxing in orders or calling a branch rep to check stock—are highly vulnerable to disruption. We defend the moat and expand margins by executing a massive digital transformation, transitioning the business into a modern, omnichannel B2B e-commerce platform.

We invest heavily in Product Information Management (PIM) systems to ensure all SKUs have rich, accurate data, high-resolution images, and robust technical specifications. We then deploy enterprise-grade e-commerce portals that integrate directly with the customer's own procurement software (via punchout catalogs). This digital shift is not just about defending market share; it is a profound cost-reduction strategy. A digital order requires zero human intervention, dramatically lowering the 'Cost to Serve' compared to a traditional inside-sales transaction.

As we migrate 20%, 30%, or 40% of the revenue base to the e-commerce portal, we achieve incredible operating leverage. The business can scale revenue rapidly without linearly adding expensive sales headcount or building new physical branches. Furthermore, the digital platform provides massive datasets on customer browsing behavior, allowing for highly targeted, AI-driven cross-selling and up-selling. A distributor with a world-class digital storefront commands a significant multiple premium at exit due to its scalability and defense against disruption.
